Audience: every first-time Wisconsin Class D applicant, since new drivers face Wisconsin winters and rural roads with farm traffic from their first season.
Why it matters to a first-timer: the chapter covers icy-road spotting, braking without ABS and hydroplaning [A01], and skid recovery, winter driving, snowplows and rural hazards [A02].
Level: short procedures plus a few exact values; light load but several look-alike emergency responses.
Prerequisites: the basics sections on speed, stopping and space, and the lights rules in the communication pages.
